1: # TheBoringTV for LG webOS
2: 
3: A Google TV-style home screen for LG webOS TVs. It's a plain HTML/CSS/JS web app with no build step.
4: 
5: Built and tested on an LG 55UR8040 (webOS 25, SDK 10.3, Chromium 120) at 1920x1080. Works with the arrow keys,
6: OK and Back, the Magic Remote pointer, and the scroll wheel.
7: 
8: ![Home screen with the featured title and Top picks](docs/screenshots/01-home.jpg)
9: 
10: | Rows with a blurred background | Details page with where to watch |
11: |:---:|:---:|
12: | ![Popular on Netflix, JioHotstar and Prime Video rows](docs/screenshots/02-rows.jpg) | ![Details page with Watch, Trailer and Watchlist buttons](docs/screenshots/03-details.jpg) |
13: | **Search across services** | **Quick settings** |
14: | ![Search with on-screen keyboard and where-to-watch labels](docs/screenshots/04-search.jpg) | ![Quick settings side panel](docs/screenshots/05-quick-settings.jpg) |
15: | **Settings** | **Profiles** |
16: | ![Settings panel with country, languages and services](docs/screenshots/06-settings.jpg) | ![Who's watching profile picker](docs/screenshots/07-profiles.jpg) |
17: | **Ambient mode** | |
18: | ![Ambient mode slideshow with clock](docs/screenshots/08-ambient.jpg) | |
19: 
20: ## Features
21: - **Hero and rows:** full-screen featured titles, "Top picks", "Popular on Netflix / JioHotstar / Prime Video" and
22:   "Trending on YouTube", using [TMDB](https://www.themoviedb.org/) and the YouTube Data API.
23: - **Where to watch:** pressing OK on a title opens a details page with "Watch on …" buttons for the services that
24:   stream it in your country, a trailer, cast and "More like this".
25: - **Watchlist, Continue watching:** both saved on the TV. Netflix and Hotstar don't share watch history, so
26:   Continue watching lists the titles you opened from this home screen.
27: - **Search across services:** an on-screen keyboard; each result shows where it's streaming.
28: - **Your apps:** checks a list of known apps (webOS won't list installed apps to non-system apps) and opens them.
29: - **Settings:** country, recommendation languages (pick several), which services get rows, clock, and more.
30: - **Quick settings panel:** Wi-Fi, audio output, Bluetooth, volume, screensaver and inputs.
31: - **Profiles:** each has its own settings, watchlist and history, plus a kids profile.
32: - **Ambient mode:** a slideshow of artwork with the clock when the TV is idle.
33: 
34: ## Setup
35: 1. Copy `keys.example.js` to `keys.js` and add a free TMDB API key and a YouTube Data API v3 key.
36:    `keys.js` is gitignored.
37: 2. Set your region, services and apps in `config.js`.
38: 3. Preview it in a browser:
39:    ```bash
40:    python3 -m http.server 8765
41:    ```
42:    Then open http://localhost:8765 in a 1920x1080 window. Use the arrow keys, Enter, and Esc (Esc acts as Back).
43: 
44: ## Install on the TV
45: Turn on LG's Developer Mode (or use a rooted TV), install the [webOS CLI](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webos-tools/cli),
46: and add your TV with `ares-setup-device`. Then:
47: ```bash
48: ares-package . -o /tmp --no-minify
49: ```
50: ```bash
51: ares-install --device tv /tmp/com.boring.tvhome_*.ipk
52: ```
53: ```bash
54: ares-launch --device tv com.boring.tvhome
55: ```
56: Developer Mode installs expire after 50 hours unless you extend them in the Developer Mode app.
57: 
58: ## Make it the real home screen (rooted TVs)
59: On a TV rooted with the [Homebrew Channel](https://github.com/webosbrew/webos-homebrew-channel), there are two options.
60: To root a TV, see [e.nya.je/getroot](https://e.nya.je/getroot/) (at your own risk: it may void your warranty, and a firmware update can remove root).
61: Both live in `service/`, are packaged with the app, and change no files on disk.
62: 
63: **Replace LG's home (recommended).** `service/as-home.sh` runs early at every boot. It copies TV Home into RAM, gives
64: the copy LG home's app id (`com.webos.app.home`), bind-mounts it over LG's home, and restarts the app manager so it
65: picks the copy up. webOS then opens TV Home wherever it would open LG's home: the Home button, Back from an app, and
66: startup (the script also opens it at boot, so the TV no longer starts on the Live TV no-signal screen).
67: ```bash
68: ares-package . service -e service -e docs -e .git -o /tmp --no-minify
69: ```
70: ```bash
71: ares-install --device tvroot /tmp/com.boring.tvhome_*.ipk
72: ```
73: ```bash
74: ssh root@<tv-ip> 'ln -sf /media/developer/apps/usr/palm/services/com.boring.tvhome.service/as-home.sh /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/40-tvhome-as-home && reboot'
75: ```
76: It also sets the TV's "last input" to TV Home, so boots that would open Live TV ("Not Programmed" without an antenna)
77: open TV Home's loading screen instead (the original value is saved in `/var/lib/webosbrew/tvhome-last-input.orig`).
78: It also turns off LG's *Home Auto Launch*, so a power cut behaves like a restart: a black screen, then TV Home's
79: loading screen, and LG's own home never shows. The trade-off is that webOS's boot animation no longer plays (it only
80: runs on the Home Auto Launch path, which would otherwise open LG's home before the swap).
81: 
82: Undo: `rm /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/40-tvhome-as-home`, set the last input back to Live TV with
83: `luna-send -n 1 luna://com.webos.settingsservice/setSystemSettings '{"category":"general","settings":{"lastInputApp":"com.webos.app.livetv","physicalLastInputApp":"com.webos.app.livetv","homeAutoLaunch":"on"}}'`,
84: and restart the TV. The script also hides the regular TV Home
85: app from the app list (another RAM-only mount), so before installing an update run
86: `ssh root@<tv-ip> 'umount /media/developer/apps/usr/palm/applications/com.boring.tvhome/appinfo.json'`.
87: 
88: After a power cut, webOS shows the last input for the first ~50 seconds until the script can run; with the setting
89: above that's TV Home's loading screen. Turning the TV on with the remote doesn't do a cold boot
90: when Quick Start+ is on (Settings → General → Devices → TV Management), so it comes straight back to TV Home. The running copy is TV Home as it was
91: at the last boot, so restart after updating TV Home. TV Home running as the home app keeps its own settings and
92: history, separate from the regular TV Home app.
93: 
94: **Or watch the Home key.** `service/service.js` reads the remote without grabbing it and opens TV Home after each Home
95: press, at startup and after standby. LG's home still flashes briefly and Back from apps still goes to LG's home.
96: ```bash
97: ssh root@<tv-ip> 'D=/media/developer/apps/usr/palm/services/com.boring.tvhome.service; ln -sf $D/autostart.sh /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/50-tvhome && sh $D/autostart.sh'
98: ```
99: Use one option, not both. `HOME_CODE` in `service/service.js` is 773 on LG Magic Remotes; raise `HOME_DELAYS` if
100: LG's home still covers TV Home.
101: 
102: ## Rooted extras: real apps, picture and sound, inputs, remote control
103: With the service running (rooted TV), it also gives TV Home what a normal app can't get. It runs as root and
104: calls a fixed list of system methods, which the page reaches over the TV's loopback (`127.0.0.1:45620`):
105: - **Your apps** shows every installed app with its real icon, not the list in `config.js`.
106: - **Quick settings** gets picture mode, sound mode, brightness, a row of inputs (HDMI names, connected ones
107:   first) and **Screen off**, which keeps audio playing; any remote key turns the screen back on.
108: 
109: `tools/tv` controls the TV from your computer over SSH:
110: ```bash
111: export TV_IP=192.168.1.50 TV_MAC=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff   # your TV; the MAC is only needed for "on"
112: tools/tv volume 20        # or up, down, mute, unmute
113: tools/tv input hdmi1
114: tools/tv launch netflix   # tools/tv apps lists ids
115: tools/tv picture cinema   # backlight 0-100, sound movie, screen-off, home, off, on, status
116: ```
117: For Home Assistant, its built-in **LG webOS Smart TV** integration already controls power, volume, inputs and apps
118: over the TV's own network API, with no root needed. Use `tools/tv` (from a shell command) for the extras.
119: 
120: ## Deep links
121: "Watch on …" opens the exact title, using the link format each app accepts (Prime's and JioHotstar's were captured
122: from LG's own voice search):
123: 
124: | Service | Id source | Link sent as `contentTarget` |
125: |---|---|---|
126: | Netflix | Wikidata (P1874) | `m=https://www.netflix.com/title/<id>&source_type=4` |
127: | Prime Video | Prime's search page, via the service (rooted TV) | the Amazon title id, `amzn1.dv.gti.…` |
128: | JioHotstar | JustWatch, matched by TMDB id, then Wikidata (P11049) | `https://livingroom.hotstar.com/<id>` |
129: | YouTube | the video id | `https://www.youtube.com/tv?v=<id>` |
130: 
131: Ids are cached on the TV. If a lookup finds nothing or takes too long, the app just opens normally.
132: 
133: ## Limits
134: - Without root it's an app, not the system launcher: the Home button opens LG's home.
135: - webOS still shows a short splash (TV Home's own dark one) when it has to start TV Home from scratch.
136: - Deep links need each service's own title id, so a title opens the app's home when no id is found.
137: - The app can't read LG Channels' channel list or Netflix/Hotstar watch history.
138: 
139: ## Credits
140: App icons in `icons/`, the webOS launch approach and the Home-button service in `service/` come from
141: [zzeppieri/webos-custom-home](https://github.com/zzeppieri/webos-custom-home) (MIT licence). Title data and images
142: come from TMDB; this product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
143: 
144: ## Feature files
145: Each feature lives in `features/<name>.js` + `features/<name>.css` and only talks to the core through `window.TV`
146: (defined at the end of `app.js`). `profiles.js` loads *before* `app.js`; the others load after it.
147: 
148: | API | What it does |
149: |---|---|
150: | `TV.addView(name, {nav, show, hide, onFocus?, back?, keydown?})` | Full-screen/overlay screen. `nav()` returns rows of focusable elements (give them class `f`; focused one gets `.focus`). Arrow keys, OK, pointer and wheel then work automatically. `back()` overrides Back (default: `TV.closeView()`). `keydown(ev)` runs first on every key while the view is open; return `true` to swallow it. |
151: | `TV.openView(name, arg)` / `TV.closeView()` | Push / pop a view; closing restores the previous focus. |
152: | `TV.rebuild(r?, c?)` | Re-read `nav()` after the view's content changes (optionally move focus). |
153: | `TV.addTab(label, viewName)` | Adds a top-bar tab that opens a view. |
154: | `TV.addRow(fn)` + `TV.refresh()` | `fn()` returns `{title, items}` or `null`; shown after Continue watching. |
155: | `TV.itemOk = fn(item)` | Called on OK for any title card / hero. Default `TV.openItem(item)` (open the service). |
156: | `TV.onAvatar = fn()` | What the avatar does (default: quick settings panel). |
157: | `TV.addSetting(row, default)` | Adds a row to the Settings panel: `{key, title, hint?, many?, opts: [[value, label]…]}`. Value lands in `TV.S[key]`. |
